k5j07jg.why: Socrates defined it as touching the Good.
k5j07jg.ask: Socrates defined it as touching the Good.
k5j07jg.bare: ___ defined it as touching the Good.
alts: He is her model of ___ man.

qo8ahkt.q: What, in Athena's account, did Socrates call philosophy?
qo8ahkt.explain: A path of education governed and led by eros: for truth, for freedom.

ildgqvx.image: Socrates as an Olympic athlete on the day of the Games
ildgqvx.meaning: Death as the performance philosophy trains for

q1481r79.q: What verb does she use for the goal of philosophy, touching truth experientially?
q1481r79.explain: The touch is tangible yet dimensionless like Euclid's point.

tf8wmnwi.s: She reads Socrates' daimonion as telling him to become a kithara player.
tf8wmnwi.explain: It meant: learn to harmonise opposites.

q1ur4bdc.q: What is her second definition of philosophy?
q1ur4bdc.explain: It complements the first, the practice of dying.

enc7s2x.reading: Insight is conceived in awareness and born as a realisation, the root of concept.

q1csfcyf.q: How does Greek philosophy treat eros, unlike paths of renunciation?
q1csfcyf.a: Know it, live it and apply it under a wisdom teaching
wrong: Avoid it as a fire that burns
Leave it to poets and dramatists
q1csfcyf.explain: With tools and criteria, so as not to be burned.

kkhyx3j.why: His not-knowing is the start of knowledge
kkhyx3j.ask: His not-knowing is the start of knowledge
kkhyx3j.bare: His ___ is the start of knowledge

xjl0rhf.author: Heraclitus of Ephesus
xjl0rhf.label: All things are one
xjl0rhf.translation: It is wise to hearken, not to me, but to my Word, and to confess that all things are one.
xjl0rhf.translator: John Burnet, Early Greek Philosophy (2nd ed. 1908; Bywater numbering)
xjl0rhf.reading: She calls this the founding principle of Hellenism: the One manifests in all and all is one. Set against the diversity the senses report, it creates the aporia of the one and the many from which Presocratic philosophy was born.

qakovnc.q: Which virtue does she name as goddess Athena's first?
qakovnc.explain: Accompanied by justice, temperance and discernment.

e4r284t.reading: Admitting 'I do not know' opens the soul's pores.

q1rf5bwy.q: According to the Call, what were the Humanities originally for?
q1rf5bwy.a: Tending the spiritual and intangible dimensions of human life
q1rf5bwy.explain: She links their decline to the loss of this purpose.

q14qrbq2.q: What does Plato say knowledge separated from justice and virtue is?

tfm1m83p.s: She claims Greek can be translated without loss, like any language.
tfm1m83p.explain: Like Beethoven or a mantra, it cannot truly be translated.

w1c1di42.q: Who am I, why am I here, and what is existence for?

alts: He is her model of ___ man.

q1ummdw8.q: Which verb means both 'to touch' and 'to kindle'?

imkj5j6.image: A marathon, an Olympic victor in training
imkj5j6.meaning: Self-knowledge is lifelong athletics that never stops.

e1tspv4r.reading: Technique is a way of giving birth.

k1v8jge4.why: He defines philosophy as erotic pedagogy and as liberation from the cave.
k1v8jge4.ask: He defines ___ as erotic pedagogy and as liberation from the cave.
k1v8jge4.bare: He defines ___ as erotic pedagogy and as liberation from the cave.
alts: True education is ___ education from childhood

wjlmjph.q: Why would Plato leave the prisoners' hands free?

q1opmt55.q: In what order do Plato's three similes appear?
q1opmt55.explain: The Sun gives the key for ascent from the sensible.

sjbry2g.title: Plato's three similes
steps: Sun
Line
Cave
sjbry2g.note: The Sun comes first to give a key for ἀναγωγή, the ascent from the sensible to the intelligible; the Cave then summarises the whole path.

xh50bfu.work: Commentaries on Plato (Republic, Timaeus) and Platonic Theology
xh50bfu.author: Proclus
xh50bfu.ref: Chaldean Oracle on the "naked" soul, quoted by Proclus (passage not located)
xh50bfu.label: Ascent by analysis: the naked soul
xh50bfu.reading: The soul descends by synthesis, adding foreign tunics until it forms the rigid bond of death, and ascends by analysis, removing what does not belong to it, until "as the oracle says" it becomes naked (γυμνῆτις) and unites with the immaterial forms.

beats.beat: Socrates says he is no teacher but a midwife, like his mother Phaenarete.
beats.reading: All souls are pregnant with the true self.

beats.beat: He calls on Artemis to help you give birth to what you carry.
beats.reading: The highest pregnancy is of the true self, the 'birth of light'.

d1757lpq.point: Socrates did not teach; he helped pregnant souls give birth.

x1fh4zsn.author: Plotinus
x1fh4zsn.label: A presence greater than knowledge
x1fh4zsn.translation: The principal cause of our uncertainty is that our comprehension of the One comes to us neither by scientific knowledge, nor by thought, as the knowledge of other intelligible things, but by a presence which is superior to science. When the soul acquires the scientific knowledge of something, she withdraws from unity and ceases being entirely one; for science implies discursive reason and discursive reason implies manifoldness. ... Instruction, indeed, goes as far as showing the road, and guiding us in the way; but to obtain the vision (of the divinity), is the work suitable to him who has desired to obtain it.
x1fh4zsn.reading: Stopping at intellectual knowledge is "a hindrance and not a fruition of philosophy": awareness of the One comes by a presence greater than knowledge, because reasoning is multiple. She compares it to Socrates' "I know that I know nothing" and to Tao Te Ching 71.

tfzljftu.s: She notes that 'know thyself' is in the singular.
tfzljftu.explain: Not 'know yourselves': it points to one Self.

qmfk5o9.q: Why, for Athena, is 'know thyself' a riddle?
qmfk5o9.a: You already are yourself, and to be something is the highest knowing
wrong: The Pythia spoke it in verse
No one knows who wrote it
qmfk5o9.explain: Like telling a cat to know what it is to be a cat: it already is.

ica0gr7.image: Telling a cat to know what it is to be a cat
ica0gr7.meaning: You already are what 'know thyself' asks you to know: being something is the highest knowing.

dl0xh0t.point: The elided inscription may allow 'know it': know the only thing that exists.

q1g7zy31.q: What was Socrates' practical test of any inquiry?
q1g7zy31.a: ποία χρεία; what use is it?

beats.beat: During the campaign Socrates stands all night in meditation.
beats.reading: Proof he was a contemplative, not a dry rationalist.

beats.beat: At dawn he salutes the sun, then goes to fight for Athens.
beats.reading: Realisation and civic duty go together.

q8k5kea.q: Socrates calls illness an inner what?
q8k5kea.explain: Health is a form of inner peace.

q1w0kcn9.q: In the Theaetetus, with whom does Socrates say he speaks?
q1w0kcn9.a: Only with those who are pregnant in soul
wrong: Only with those who have studied geometry
q1w0kcn9.explain: His maieutic art needs a gestation already begun.

qo53lb3.q: Where does she place Socrates as a mystic?
qo53lb3.explain: His anthropocentric turn brought realisation into ethics and politics.

qblrpqp.q: What did Socrates do at Potidaea, as she tells it?
qblrpqp.a: Stood meditating all night, then saluted the sun
qblrpqp.explain: Then he went to fight for Athens.

q19ikoe5.q: What does she say Socrates was, rather than a teacher?
q19ikoe5.explain: He spoke only with souls he saw were pregnant.

qaf0pfq.q: What name does Socrates give the path, in her account?
qaf0pfq.explain: The central path of Greek philosophy.

tfug1mjh.s: She says she added the five modes to Plato's text herself.
tfug1mjh.explain: She says she decodes them from the text.

beats.beat: In the Republic, intellectual truth is the light.
beats.reading: Knowledge illuminates, but it is not the source.

beats.beat: The Good, or the One, is the Sun, the source of reason and mind.
beats.reading: The end of knowledge is to move beyond knowledge into its source.

i1v6f56n.image: The East as a cleanser of the lens
i1v6f56n.meaning: Eastern practice let her read Plato with new eyes

dxg7ixl.point: Plato asked us to walk the path, not only to talk about it.

eizn68v.reading: Plato's puppeteers; she hears the same word in today's spiritual wonder-mongering, and finds the true wonder-maker in the mind.

wg2cvu2.q: Plato and Jesus both said walk the path; why do we now only talk about it?

q1hdbt97.q: What does the story of Helen show, in her reading?
q1hdbt97.a: Only her phantom went to Troy
wrong: She was a goddess in disguise
She returned to Sparta at once
q1hdbt97.explain: The world of images was known before Plato.

xmvr3c3.work: Commentaries on Plato (Republic, Timaeus) and Platonic Theology
xmvr3c3.author: Proclus
xmvr3c3.label: The one transcendent cause
xmvr3c3.reading: Quoted in the description of her talk on the One: before all beings and gods there is one transcendent, unparticipated cause, ineffable, unknowable and ungraspable, which Socrates calls the Good (through the Sun) and Parmenides the One (through negations).

tflx0whg.s: She draws on Plato's Sun analogy to present truth as the light that makes knowing possible.
tflx0whg.explain: Republic 507 to 509: the Good as sun, the soul's eye, and truth as light.

beats.beat: Diogenes walks around naked, urinates in the agora and hits people with his staff.
beats.reading: Awakened sages do not fit a respectable template.

beats.beat: Plato the aristocrat, Socrates the family man, hermits and illiterate shepherds were also sages.
beats.reading: History offers wildly different sages so that we cannot dogmatise awakening.

beats.beat: The eagle-mother pushes her chicks out of the nest so they fly.
beats.reading: Being and nature do not let awakened souls stay above; they are pushed back into becoming.

beats.beat: Plato says the freed will not be allowed to stay above.
beats.reading: Answers from her audience: to awaken others, to consolidate, to practise, to complete the cycle, to see all is one.

e1bwzaic.reading: The elided form may allow 'know it': know the only thing that exists, the one Self.

s1fpjns2.title: Two stages of γνῶθι σαυτόν
steps: Know your preferences, personality, body, mind, heart and desires: the three parts of the soul
Know 'that which knows': the observer itself
s1fpjns2.note: The first stage is valid but Apollo asks more: you are not what you have.

tf1266h93.s: She attributes Know thyself and the E to Apollo himself, and the other precepts to the Seven Sages.
tf1266h93.explain: Two precepts are Apollo's own in her account.

q1crxgt.q: What alternative reading of 'know thyself' does she suggest?
q1crxgt.explain: The elided inscription may allow it.

q1hsu4le.q: What does she say is the final meaning of γνῶθι σαυτόν?
wrong: Know your limits as a mortal
q1hsu4le.explain: Knowing the personality is stage one; the knower is the goal.

pxl6rk3.title: Ask 'ποία χρεία;'
steps: Of any knowledge, ask what use it has
Ask what it changes in lived experience
pxl6rk3.why: Socrates disliked idle philosophising; knowledge must serve life.

ph7tn9l.title: Know your three selves
steps: Tell the story of your small self: birthplace, degrees, relationships
Study your soul's faculties: mind, heart, will, appetite
Seek the secret self, yourself as the One
ph7tn9l.why: Self-knowledge moves inward like a walk into a temple.

p3xi2fn.title: Admit that you do not know
steps: Recognise honestly that you do not know
Let that make you ask, as the restless prisoner asks whether things are as he was told
p3xi2fn.why: Asking opens the pores (ἀπορία), and Apollo begins to reveal himself.

p1q0uhke.title: Practise aporia
steps: Start from 'I do not know'
Set aside prior knowledge
Do not turn truth into a banner
p1q0uhke.why: Renouncing knowledge is the beginning of knowledge.

p1tlkdcj.title: Let pain become a gate
steps: Treat psychic pain like training: it hurts, and leads to no pain
Let it push you out of the state you are in
Let it wake light and freedom in you
p1tlkdcj.why: Pain presses, and can become a gate of liberation.

p90gdv1.title: Train with a sensible example
steps: Take something visible: sunlight, the eye, a solstice
Use it as a παράδειγμα to grasp the invisible
p90gdv1.why: Plato's ἀναγωγή climbs from the sensible to the intelligible.

p11d3p6z.title: Hear 'know thyself' now
steps: Hear or say the words: know thyself
Notice the small pause they make in the mind
Turn the eye of the mind from outside to inside
Stop looking at anything but your own essence
p11d3p6z.why: Athena calls the maxim the shortest way to the μεταστροφή that Socrates calls paideia.
